subject: Clarifying throughput & latency constraints to recommend deployment mode
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.example.com>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha@vectorhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + 2 follow-ups from today's deployment conversation

Hi Aisha —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap of what I heard and a couple of asks so we can nail the recommendation: 

Summary from our call:
- Workload: real-time event enrichment pipeline (post-processing of user activity) feeding downstream feature stores and notifications.
- SLOs you mentioned: p95 response target in the 150–250 ms range for most enrichment requests; p99 not to exceed ~400 ms for single-token generations.
- Typical steady-state QPS: ~80–120 across the US production region; predictable daily peak up to ~180–220 QPS with occasional bursts (~250 QPS) for flash-events.
- Payload characteristics: prompt size small (avg 120 tokens), some longer requests up to 600 tokens for debugging/analytics.
- Data residency: US-only; no immediate on-prem requirement.

Initial asks I need from you to finalize a deployment path (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private):
1) Can you confirm p95 and p99 targets in milliseconds (number preferred) for the event enrichment path vs ad-hoc analytics?
2) For peak bursts, do you expect sustained 200+ QPS for more than 30 minutes, or are bursts typically <10 minutes?
3) Any procurement constraints (PO terms, approval lead time) we should factor into timelines?

Attached: initial-latency-estimates.csv — a basic matrix I put together to show how p95 shifts with batching and caching assumptions.

Next steps I propose once you confirm the numbers above:
- If p95 requirement is <=200ms and sustained QPS <200: Hosted API with targeted autoscaling and prefix caching is likely the fastest path.
- If p95 needs to be <=175ms at sustained QPS >200 (or predictable heavy sustained load), Dedicated reserved capacity with a small burst pool will be better for consistent tail latency and throughput.
- We can schedule a 30-minute technical deep-dive with our infra team to walk the exact kernel/quantization tradeoffs if you want a Dedicated sizing exercise.

Would love the three datapoints above and a good time for the technical deep-dive (I have windows Thurs and next Tue afternoon PT).

Best,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
diego@redwood.example.com

From: Aisha Shah <aisha@vectorhealth.com>

Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + 2 follow-ups from today's deployment conversation

Diego —

Thanks for the summary — good capture. Answers inline: 

1) p95 / p99 targets:
- Event enrichment (primary): p95 <= 220 ms, p99 <= 380 ms. This path is latency-sensitive but tolerates up to ~380ms at the extreme.
- Ad-hoc analytics / debugging: p95 <= 800 ms (not latency-critical).

2) Burst behavior:
- Bursts to 200–250 QPS happen roughly once per week, typically lasting 5–12 minutes. We have occasional traffic spikes (marketing-driven) that can sustain ~120–150 QPS for 1–2 hours.

3) Procurement:
- Standard PO process, ~4–6 weeks once SOW/quote is approved. We can start contractual discussions in parallel to technical validation.

Extras: we do prefer Hosted for speed of onboarding, but reliability and consistent tail latency are more important than launch speed. If Dedicated gives a clear latency improvement at sustained load, we'll lean that way.

Aisha
Aisha Shah
VP Engineering — VectorHealth
aisha@vectorhealth.com

Subject: Recommendation: Dedicated reserved capacity with canary + hosted fallback (based on your targets)

Aisha —

Appreciate the clarifications — that helps a lot. Given the p95/p99 targets and burst profile you shared, our recommended path is:

1) Short term (fast start): Enable Hosted API for non-critical lanes (analytics, debugging) and run a lightweight canary for enrichment traffic for 1–2 weeks. This gets you live quickly and gives us real telemetry on request size distribution.

2) Medium-term (recommended): Dedicated reserved capacity sized to handle steady-state 120–150 QPS with a burst pool sized for 250 QPS. Key config notes:
- Reserve GPU pool with 20–25% headroom (we'll size after telemetry) so p95 stays under 200–220 ms for avg prompts.
- Autoscaling policy tuned for short bursts (scale up within ~30s) and a small warm pool for cold-starts.
- Prefix/KV caching turned on for enrichment (your prompts show a lot of reuse across events). This reduces per-token work and improves tail.
- Canary rollout and automatic fallback to hosted variants if saturation occurs — keeps service online during edge cases.

3) Sizing and cost: I'm attaching a more detailed capacity-recommendation-v2.pdf and a preliminary cost-estimate-quote.xlsx. These assume gpt-variant pricing and two sizing scenarios (conservative vs aggressive).

Technical tradeoffs we discussed that favor Dedicated here:
- Deterministic tail latency at sustained QPS because you control the reserved pool.
- Easier to enforce low-latency kernels / quantization profiles without noisy multi-tenant neighbors.

If you want, Karthik (cc'd) can run through the specifics — kernel/sequence length breakdown — on the technical deep-dive. Proposed times: Tue 2026-09-08 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu 2026-09-10 13:00–13:30 PT.

Next steps we recommend:
- You confirm preferred deep-dive slot and internal stakeholders to invite (infra + procurement).
- We'll provision a temporary canary on Hosted and start collecting telemetry (no cost to run the canary for the first 72 hours).
- We'll prepare an SOW and formal quote in parallel so procurement has something to review.

Best,
Diego
